The first UTF-16 unit (c0) of each starter is used as the array index, even for surrogate-pair starters. This design matches the existing dense-table layout and ensures fast O(1) access without hashing.

If future datasets include astral phrases, the existing layout remains safe—it will simply probe a few extra candidate lengths.
Using pre-deserialized masks avoids rescanning every dictionary key and typically saves 5–15 ms of startup time for large OpenCC dictionaries.

remarks.para: This internal normalizer loads the curated mappings from the assembly's embedded Unicode_Compatibility.txt resource. The table contains selected Unicode radicals, glyph variants, punctuation forms, and known text-extraction artifacts that are useful when normalizing CJK text.

Every mapping is strictly one Unicode scalar value to one Unicode scalar value. Length-expanding or length-contracting mappings are rejected when the table is loaded. member.name: M:OpenccNetLib.UnicodeCompat.LoadExtendedPages
member.summary: Loads the curated Unicode compatibility mapping table into a sparse paged lookup structure.
member.remarks:
Each non-comment line must contain exactly two tab-separated columns: one non-ASCII source Unicode scalar and one target Unicode scalar.
Pages are allocated lazily in blocks of 256 code points. This avoids dictionary lookup overhead during normalization while keeping memory usage proportional to the Unicode regions actually used by the mapping table.
ASCII source mappings are rejected to prevent accidental rewriting of markup and structured-text syntax, including XML and OpenXML content. Invalid rows fail fast so bundled mapping mistakes cannot be silently ignored.

member.exception: A mapping row is malformed, contains an invalid Unicode scalar, contains too many columns, or uses an ASCII source character.
